A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the subtraction errors of foregrounds in the EOR observations are not only determined by the foreground-removing techniques themselves, but also by the interactions between the subtraction techniques, the array configurations, and the data analysis methods.
the subtraction errors for each foreground-removal technique are not only dependent on the characteristics of the foregrounds but also the characteristics of the EOR signal.
we can improve foreground subtraction in the statistical observations of the EOR by using all the foreground subtraction techniques that have been proposed so far in combination.

a combination of different foreground-techniques is required to reduce the EOR contamination to a level where the EOR signal can be revealed.
the foreground-removing algorithms should be used in a specific order to maximize the signal-to-noise of the EOR signal.
